channel_notes: Historia Civilis uses a distinctive minimalist animated style. Thumbnails follow a highly consistent template: large serif/display text (usually the video title) occupying most of the frame, with a circular inset vignette showing an animated scene from the video (battle formations as colored squares, maps with territory shading, or simple props). No talking head, no creator face. The channel's signature is colored squares representing armies/people on simplified terrain maps.

summary.design_pattern_notes: Historia Civilis has one of the most consistent thumbnail templates in the edu/history niche. Nearly every thumbnail follows the same formula: (1) Large serif/display text covering 60-80% of the frame with the video title, (2) a circular inset vignette (usually right side or bottom center) showing an animated scene from the video, (3) flat color or pattern background matching the era/mood. The circular inset is the channel's signature element - it always has a thick colored border (matching the text color) and contains the channel's minimalist animated style: colored squares for armies, simplified terrain maps, or abstract scene representations. No creator face ever appears. The 4 faces that appear are all ancient sculptures or historical portrait paintings (Congress of Vienna, Alexander, Philip II). Text is ALWAYS present and dominates. Zero logos or watermarks.
